provenance.paper_title: Long-Horizon Embodied Decision-Making via Multimodal Memory Compression

evidence.section: Full paper: Multimodal Memory of Embodied Agent
evidence.paraphrase: A fixed number of memory tokens compress decision-relevant multimodal history conditioned on user preferences.

The trained compressor continually replaces long raw history with compact memory tokens. For MeMento, this specifically supports a trained but frozen update module of preference-conditioned compressed multimodal history.

Long-horizon evidence is abstracted into preference-relevant decision state. For MeMento, this specifically supports abstraction of episodes into reusable experience of preference-conditioned compressed multimodal history.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (PDF p. 8): During inference, the operative memory component (preference-conditioned compressed multimodal history) changes through a trained but frozen update module, abstraction of episodes into reusable experience; the governing policy remains fixed, and any learning reported by the paper occurs before deployment. Training-time learning, when present, was not counted as T3.
